_comment: CI wall-clock budgets for .github/workflows/ci.yml, enforced by the
'CI wall-clock budget' job via scripts/check_ci_wall_clock.py (issue
#1971). Budgets are in SECONDS and were derived from the measured
baseline recorded below -- see docs/guides/ci-wall-clock-budget.md for
the full per-job breakdown, the derivation, and how to re-measure.
These are regression budgets, NOT the hard ceilings that ci.yml's
per-job `timeout-minutes` already provides. A timeout only fires once a
job blows way past budget (the `test` matrix has a 45-minute ceiling on
a job whose median is 4 minutes); these budgets fire at roughly 2x the
measured p90, which is the band where a real regression lives and
ordinary runner noise does not.
Raising a budget is a legitimate change -- say why in the PR. Silently
raising it to make a red run green is the drift this file exists to stop.
FULL RE-MEASURE, 2026-09-29 (issue #2612). Every row below and the whole
baseline block were re-derived from scratch, replacing the 2026-09-17
baseline and the four interim bumps stacked on top of it (#2225 and
#2276 guessed 300s for two then-new jobs; #1869 raised the total to
1800; #2392 raised the four Tests legs to 420 and the total to 2100).
Each of those entries said a full re-measure was still owed rather than
more headroom-on-headroom; this is it.
Why now: docs/guides/ci-wall-clock-budget.md makes a re-measure
MANDATORY after a runner-pool change, and two happened without one --
the 2026-09-24 migration of the heavy jobs to Blacksmith autoscaled
runners (c66f18fd, #2214) and the 2026-09-28 move of the short and
scheduled jobs back to GitHub-hosted (6da0c9a4, #2598). The 420s Tests
budget was calibrated against a retired fixed pool and had started
failing main on unrelated diffs: 8 of 72 sampled main-push runs had at
least one Tests leg over 420s.
Sample (widened per issue #2612): 273 ci.yml runs from 2026-09-24 to
2026-09-29 -- main pushes AND same-repo PR runs, and NOT filtered to
`--status=success` runs, because excluding wall-clock-failed runs
survivor-biases the sample away from exactly the noise tail this budget
exists to tolerate. Each observation is still a job that itself
concluded `success`, and each job's numbers are taken only from runs
where that job ran on the runner label ci.yml assigns it TODAY, so the
two pool migrations above cannot blend into one distribution. The
2026-09-24 run 36003284901 (all four Tests legs at 724-816s at once, a
3401s total) is excluded as a bad-node incident rather than tolerable
noise -- and it would still breach both the per-job and the total
budget below if replayed, which is the intended behaviour.
Tests (Python 3.10)/(3.11)/(3.12)/(3.13) are 700, not 420. Pooled over
755 leg observations the four legs measure median 253s, p90 361s, p95
412s, max 996s; 2x p90 is 722s, rounded to 700 (the 2026-09-17 baseline
rounded 2x194=388 down to 360 the same way). All four share one budget
because they are the same suite differing only by interpreter. 700 is
also the knee of the in-sample false-breach curve: every ceiling from
700 to 800 leaves the same 4 of 755 legs over, so paying another 100s
of gate laxity buys nothing. At 700 the sampled main-push false-breach
rate drops from 8 of 72 runs to 2 -- one of which is the excluded
bad-node incident, leaving exactly one non-incident residual (run
36611724105 on ee8fc812, one leg at 809s). That residual is the subject
of the model caveat at the end of this comment, not a reason to buy
another 150s of laxity. This independently lands on the same
number PR #2571 picked as an interim unblock, so that bump is confirmed
by derivation rather than left standing as a placeholder -- but its
companion total of 2600 is superseded by the 3000 below.
total_job_budget_seconds is 3000, not 2100: measured over the 35 runs
that carry exactly today's job set on today's runner labels, total
compute is median 1684s, p90 2316s, max 2833s. 3000 clears the observed
max by 6% and the median by 78%. It is deliberately NOT the 3460s that
four 700s legs plus the cheap jobs could reach while every per-job
budget still passes: the total exists to catch death by a thousand
cheap jobs, so it has to bind somewhere below the sum of the per-job
ceilings.
run_wall_clock_budget_seconds stays 1800. Queue-inclusive wall clock
over the same 35 runs is median 477s, p90 820s, max 1006s, so 1800
still has room; it is also the only threshold whose breach does not
fail the build (a queue breach reports and exits 0), so leaving it
where it is keeps a live signal on pool contention. The autoscaled pool
does queue deeper than the retired one under burst -- one sampled PR
run waited 33 minutes for two Blacksmith legs (2255s wall on 1633s of
compute) -- and that is precisely the annotation this threshold should
keep emitting.
Golden artifacts (hash seed + path varied) and Tests (numpy
cross-check) are 120, not the 300 first guessed for them by #2225 and
#2276: both now have real timings (p90 19s/20s, max 54s/32s) and both
land under the 120s floor every sub-60s job gets. 'examples/signoff
round-trip' (#2163) gains its first row at that same floor -- it was
silently inheriting the 600s default_job_budget_seconds.
Two rows moved with the pools rather than with the code: 'Native
engines (Rust) - static timing' is 150, not 120, because 6da0c9a4 moved
it from Blacksmith to GitHub-hosted (p90 43s -> 64s, 2x p90 = 128s),
and 'Native engines (Rust)' holds 240 rather than dropping to the 200
its 2x p90 of 182s would suggest: its sibling legs on the same
Blacksmith pool show max/p90 ratios up to 3.4x, so a 200s ceiling would
measure the pool. 240 is still 1.8x its observed 136s max.
MODEL CAVEAT (design note, no code change here -- see the guide's
'Is a fixed per-job ceiling still the right model?'): on an autoscaled
pool the Tests legs' noise tail is now wider than the regression signal
this gate is meant to catch, so a fixed per-leg ceiling loose enough to
be quiet (700s) can no longer notice a 2x slowdown of the 253s median.
The fix is a better statistic, not a bigger number -- spikes are
single-leg (worst runs read 439/442/459/996 and 314/317/394/923) while
a real regression moves all four together, as the excluded incident's
724/741/810/816 shows. Changing the statistic is out of scope for this
re-measure.

baseline.sample: 273 ci.yml runs from 2026-09-24 to 2026-09-29 (main pushes and same-repo PR runs, success AND failure conclusions); per-job numbers use only observations from the runner label ci.yml assigns that job today (n=44-273 per job, n=755 pooled across the four Tests legs); aggregates use the 35 runs carrying exactly today's job set on today's labels; the 2026-09-24 bad-node incident run 36003284901 is excluded
